newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Livestock Feeds plans price hike.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Livestock Feeds plans price hike.

text.p: Nigeria's leading manufacturer of animal feeds, Livestock Feeds, said on Thursday it planned to increase prices of its products.
A company spokesman said this was one of the measures adopted to bolster profitability.

The spokesman, who was commenting on a 71 percent drop in the company's pre-tax profits for the year ended last November 30, said 1996 saw high production costs that could not be immediately recouped from customers.
The proposed hike in product prices would help shore up its revenue base but would only be implemented when the market could absorb it, the company said.
In addition, the company said it would soon review its capital structure to strengthen its financial base.
Livestock Feeds posted 16.5 million naira profit before tax in the period from 57 million a year earlier.
Turnover, however, rose to 880.3 million naira from 685.6 million.

The company's dependence on short-term funds also weighed on profits, he said, adding, "Interest expense was high relative to 1995." Livestock Feeds said it would pay a dividend of 25 kobo per share against 20 kobo in 1995.
Panama-based Pfizer Corporation has a majority stake in the firm while the Nigerian public controls 40 percent.
